title: Linear-Time Four-Coloring and Near-Quadratic General Matching
summary: Two new preprints report major advances in graph algorithms: optimal linear-time four-coloring of planar graphs and an n^{2+o(1)}-time maximum matching algorithm for general graphs.
intro: This briefing highlights two recent algorithmic advances. Both are presented as research preprints; their proofs have not been independently checked for this post.

results.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
results.summary: A new algorithm computes a proper four-coloring of any planar graph in optimal linear time.
results.body:
**Statement.** The authors present an algorithm that computes a proper four-coloring of an $n$-vertex planar graph in $O(n)$ time.

**Improvement.** Their earlier FOCS 2026 work achieved $O(n\log n)$ time. This preprint removes the logarithmic factor, attaining an asymptotically optimal bound for explicitly producing the coloring.

**Technique.** The previous algorithm uses $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes, each of which may affect a linear fraction of the graph. The new approach preprocesses the graph in $O(n)$ time and represents it so that each suitable Kempe change can be identified and simulated in $O(n/\log n)$ amortized time. Thus, all changes can be implemented in $O(n)$ total time.

**Verification status.** This is an arXiv preprint (version 1, submitted 29 October 2026), not a claim of independent proof verification. No proof-assistant formalization is stated in the source.

results.title: Maximum Cardinality Matching in Near-Quadratic Time
results.summary: A new preprint gives an n^{2+o(1)}-time algorithm for maximum-cardinality matching in arbitrary undirected graphs.
results.body:
**Statement.** For an arbitrary undirected graph with $n$ vertices, the authors give an algorithm for maximum-cardinality matching running in $n^{2+o(1)}$ time.

**Improvement.** The result addresses general graphs, not only bipartite graphs, and gives a near-quadratic running-time bound. For comparison, the classical $O(m\sqrt n)$ combinatorial bound becomes $O(n^{5/2})$ on dense graphs.

**Technique.** The work builds on recent combinatorial maximum-flow algorithms and extends their methods to skew-symmetric flow problems, which include general-graph matching as a special case. The abstract does not provide enough detail to substantiate a more specific account of the underlying data structures or reductions.

**Verification status.** This is an arXiv preprint (version 1, submitted 29 October 2026). The result is reported as an author claim, not as an independently checked proof; no proof-assistant formalization is stated.
